 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Hasmukh D. Suthar
 Date : 05/03/2026
 Oral Judgment

1) Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 23.03.2020 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Kheda at Nadiad, (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal" for short), in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.341/2018, the appellants- original Kantaben Rameshbhai Rathod vs Ashokbhai Rameshbhai Parmar on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5850640/
1 claimants preferred present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for short).
2) Heard Mr. Nishit Bhalodi, learned counsel for the appellants - original Claimants, Mr.Chirayu Mehta, learned counsel for respondent No.3 and Mr.Vibhuti Nanavaty, learned counsel for respondent No.6.
Though served, none appears for respondent Nos.1, 2 and 4.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4965/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined 3)

It is the case of the claimants that on 15.02.2018, while the deceased Rameshbhai Babubhai Rathod being a pillion rider was going on Activa bearing No.GJ-06-CL-4191 which was driven by respondent No.4 on correct side of the road and when they reached Kanajari Chokdi for filling up Petrol in Activa, at that time, one Pick-up Van bearing No.GJ-23-V-3911 came with excessive speed and in rash and negligent manner dashed with the Activa from behind.
As a result, the deceased got serious injuries and succumbed to it.
Therefore, the claim petition was filed by the legal heirs of the deceased to get compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the opponents.

After appreciating the evidence produced on record, the learned Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.6,04,600/- along with cost and interest @ 9 % p.a.
4) The appeal is filed on limited ground of quantum and no further issue qua liability or contributory negligence is challenged.

Therefore, learned counsel for the claimant has mainly argued that, the Tribunal has erred in considering monthly income of the deceased as Rs.6000/- on notional basis as he was doing labour work and earning Rs.8,000/- p.m.
Further, the Tribunal has also erred in not properly awarding compensation under other conventional heads which are also required to be enhanced.
Hence, he has prayed to allow the appeal as prayed for.

5) Mr. Chirayu Mehta, learned counsel for the respondent No.3- Insurance Company has opposed the present appeal and submitted that, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation in absence of any evidence of income and adequate compensation is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.
Therefore, requested to dismiss the appeal.

6) Mr. Vibhuti Nanavaty, learned counsel for respondent No.6 has stated that the Tribunal has rightly exonerated respondent Nos.4 to 6 and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4965/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation.
He has therefore submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not require any interference.
7) Having considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, it appears that the appeal is filed only on the aspect of quantum and liability is not challenged.
The Insurance Company has not filed any cross-objection.
Hence, this appeal is required to be decided on the aspect of quantum only.
Alleged incident is not in dispute.
Involvement of the vehicle is also not in dispute.

In order to prove the claim, the claimant No.1 has filed an Affidavit at Exh:33, FIR at Exh:36,
Panchnama of scene of incident at Exh:37, Inquest Panchanama at Exh:38 and PM report at Exh:39.

After appreciating the evidence produced on record, the Tribunal held the offending vehicle sole Kantaben Rameshbhai Rathod vs Ashokbhai Rameshbhai Parmar on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5850640/
2 negligent relying on the decisions of the Bimla Devi Vs. HRTC reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819 and Parmeshwari Devi Vs. Amir Chand, reported in 2011 (11) SCC 635.
8)

sentences.text: The Tribunal considering the PM report at Exh:39 has considered the age of the deceased was 58 years on the date of accident.
Therefore, this Court deems fit to consider the age of the deceased as 58 years on the date of accident.

Further, as the deceased was married and having 4 dependents,
1/4th deduction as personal expenditure and living of the deceased and multiplier of 9 were considered by the learned Tribunal as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. [2009 (6) SCC 121]

sentences.text: which are just and proper.

9) As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Govind Yadav Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2012(1) TAC 1 (SC), that if no proof of income is produced on the record, then Tribunal has to consider prevalent minimum wages in absence of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4965/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined evidence of monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: Govind Yadav Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2012(1) TAC 1 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the accident occurred in the February 2018 and during that time, the deceased was doing agriculture labour work.
Therefore, considering the government approved minimum wages prevailing at the time of accident, the income is required to be considered as Rs.7,950/-.
Hence, the income of the deceased is reassessed as Rs.7,950/- per month.

Further, the Tribunal has rightly considered future prospective income of the deceased as 10%.
10)

Therefore, calculating the income of the deceased as Rs.7950/- and future prospect of 10% =
Rs.795/- which comes to Rs.8745/- and 1/4nd amount is required to be deducted as personal expenditure and living of the deceased which comes to Rs.2186/- and the net amount comes to Rs.6,559/-, which is rounded to Rs.6,560/-.

In view of above, the amount under the head of loss of future dependency is required to be reassessed as Rs.6,560/- x 12 months x 9 multiplier =
Rs.7,08,480/-.

Therefore, the appellants are entitled to get additional amount of Rs.1,73,880/-
under the head of future loss of dependency.

11) Further, the Tribunal by relying on the judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680 has awarded total Rs.30,000/- under the two conventional heads, however, this Court is of the view that amount is required to be reassessed as Rs.18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

Therefore, the appellants - original claimants are entitled for additional amount of Rs.6,300/- (i.e. Rs.18,150/- -
Rs.15,000/- = Rs.3,150/- towards loss of estate and Rs.18,150/- - Rs.15,000/- = Rs.3,150/- towards funeral expenses.
12) Further, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 and Janabai Wd/o Dinkarrao NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4965/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Ghorpade &
Ors., Vs M/s ICICI Lambord Insurance Company Ltd., reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 666, the Tribunal has committed error in awarding Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.
Therefore, the amount towards loss of consortium is reassessed as Rs.1,93,600/- for four dependents.

As Rs.6,04,600/- is already awarded by learned Tribunal, 
appellants - original claimants are entitled to get additional amount of Rs.3,33,780/- (Rs.9,38,380 - Rs.6,04,600/-) with proportionate costs and interest as awarded by the learned Tribunal.
15) Hence, present appeal is partly allowed.
The judgment and award dated 23.03.2020 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Kheda at Nadiad, in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.341/2018 stands modified to the aforesaid extent.

Record and proceedings be remitted back to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.

16) The Tribunal is directed to recover or deduct the deficit court fees on enhanced amount and thereafter disburse and release the amount in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4965/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined favour of the claimants after due verification by transferring the said amount to the account of the claimant either by RTGS or NEFT mode.
Award to be drawn accordingly.
